atomic_issue.h100.r1.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json; probe atomic.cu: one CTA, W = 1 / 4 warps, U in {8, 16, 32, 64} straight-line atomics, lanes in blocks of L same-address lanes, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs). cycles(op, L) = slope over U of the per-U median (t_e - t_s) at W = 4 / 4 (per-SM admission interval), knots L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}: ATOM <- atom: 67.6/67.6/67.6/67.6/67.9/73.9; ATOMG <- atomg: 61.6/61.6/61.6/61.6/62.1/67.8; ATOMS <- atoms: 1.3/2.2/4.0/8.1/16.1/32.3; RED <- redg: 31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6; REDG <- redg: 31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6; REDS <- reds: 1.3/2.1/4.2/8.4/17.2/34.6. Runs agree within 0.1 % everywhere, but the U = 8 point is absorbed by the in-flight queue (the sweep is not linear from U = 8), so the OLS max relative residual is above 5 % in every cell -> experimental per protocol. Diagnostic slope(W=1)/slope(W=4) at L = 1: {'redg': 0.26, 'atomg': 0.15, 'atoms': 1.0, 'reds': 1.0, 'atom': 0.17} (global atomics are a per-SM bound; shared atomics at L = 1 look per-SMSP: open engine question, kind 15 scope). Replaces the hopper.derived.atomic_same_address table (8.51 at L <= 4 rising to 37.1 at L = 32 for every class; a predecessor fit re-expressed over same-address lanes, no probe in this repository).

atomic_issue.h100.r2.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol addendum r2 (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json addenda[0]; probe atomic.cu IND = 1: instruction i of the U targets base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB + b x 128 B, no two instructions of a rep share a line, lanes in blocks of L same-address lanes so L = 1 is 32 distinct lines per instruction; U in {16, 32, 64, 128}, W = 1 / 4, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs in one job; GPU GPU-2aaf46f6-a1da-fb47-c390-6732377364b0). cycles(op, L) = (med(U=128) - med(U=64)) / 64 / 4 at W = 4, knots L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}: atomg 74.1/74.0/74.1/74.1/75.6/74.0 (experimental, steady 0.41, agree 0.0008, OLS resid 1.41); redg 32.0/32.0/32.0/32.0/32.0/32.0 (measured, steady 0.00, agree 0.0000, OLS resid 0.11); atom 79.0/79.0/79.1/79.1/80.0/79.0 (experimental, steady 0.54, agree 0.0002, OLS resid 0.87). Control (same-job r1-style same-address slope / 4, L = 1, W = 4): atomg 61.75/61.75 vs r1 61.63, redg 31.61/31.61 vs r1 31.61 -> ok. Installed (measured cells only): RED, REDG; the other classes keep r1. Finding: with 32 distinct lines per instruction the per-SM interval is not lower than the r1 same-address figure (the same-line follow-on hypothesis of full-gpu-chain-report.md 8.6 is refuted); the cost tracks the lines a warp-wide atomic touches, which the axis atomic_same_address_lanes does not see (the stream-K fixup ATOMG is 32 lanes x 4 B in ONE line) -> addendum r3 measures the lines axis. r1 values kept in the source description of atomic_issue.h100.r1.

atomic_issue.h100.r3.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol addendum r3 (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json addenda[1]; probe atomic.cu IND = 1 with block stride S: instruction i at base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB, block b of L same-address lanes at + b x S; U in {16, 32, 64, 128}, W = 1 / 4, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs in one job; GPU GPU-2aaf46f6-a1da-fb47-c390-6732377364b0). cycles = (med(U=128) - med(U=64)) / 64 / 4 at W = 4. Lines sweep (L = 1, S = 4..128 -> cache_line_count 1/2/4/8/16/32; m = measured, e = experimental per cell): atomg 5.8/11.5/23.1/46.2/55.4/74.1 (eeeeee); redg 5.0/10.0/20.0/40.0/48.0/32.0 (mmmmmm); atom 6.0/12.2/24.3/48.6/58.2/79.0 (eeeeee). Same-word sweep (S = 4, one line, L = 1/2/4/8/16/32 lanes per word): atomg 5.8/6.9/12.0/25.6/49.7/74.0 (spread 11.6); redg 5.0/6.0/8.0/16.0/32.0/32.0 (spread 5.4); atom 6.0/8.2/13.1/27.6/53.0/79.0 (spread 12.1) -> open item: a second dependence on same-word lanes (about 1 cycle per lane for redg, 2.3 for atomg) that the single-axis leaf does not carry; the installed knots are the L = 1 (all words distinct) values. Controls: r1 same-address cell ok, r2 S = 128 cells ok (redg 32.00 vs 32.0). Installed (all six knots measured): RED, REDG on axis cache_line_count (the instruction's distinct 128 B lines); ATOMG / ATOM not installed: the W = 4 sweep of returning atomics is not steady over U (increment 32->64 vs 64->128 differ by about 40 %: the per-warp return path saturates near 64 outstanding ATOMG), they keep their previous leaf (atomic_same_address_lanes axis). Finding: a coalesced warp-wide global atomic (32 lanes x 4 B in one line, the stream-K fixup / atomicAdd epilogue pattern) costs about 5-6 cycles per SM on both devices against 61.6 / 58 installed; the r1 / r2 figures were the 32-distinct-lines pattern.

atomic_issue.h100.r5.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol addendum r5 (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json addenda[3]; probe atomic.cu IND = 1, W = 16 warps (four per SMSP), block stride S, instruction i at base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB, U in {16, 32, 64}, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs in one job; GPU GPU-f266a6de-37fb-c58b-e769-cd3e7b3a6e93). cycles = mean over U in {32, 64} of T(U) / U / 16 (saturated per-SM interval; gate flat <= 10 %, run agreement <= 5 %). Lines sweep (L = 1, S = 4..128 -> cache_line_count 1/2/4/8/16/32): atomg 4.6/9.3/18.7/37.1/44.3/56.7 (flat max 0.029, agree max 0.0020); atom 4.7/9.5/18.9/37.3/44.7/58.3 (flat max 0.037, agree max 0.0022); redg 4.6/9.4/18.9/38.0/45.7/30.6 (flat max 0.034, agree max 0.0006) (control vs the r3 REDG install: 1 lines 4.63 vs r3 5.0, 2 lines 9.44 vs r3 10.0, 4 lines 18.94 vs r3 20.0, 8 lines 38.01 vs r3 40.0, 16 lines 45.67 vs r3 48.0, 32 lines 30.58 vs r3 32.0). Same-word sweep (S = 4, one line, L lanes per word 1/2/4/8/16/32): atomg 4.6/5.7/9.4/20.2/40.8/58.2 (spread 11.6); atom 4.7/6.2/10.0/21.1/41.8/59.7 (spread 11.7); redg 4.6/5.7/7.7/15.3/30.6/30.7 (spread 5.6) -> open item carried from r3 (second dependence on same-word lanes, about 2.3 cycles per lane for atomg; the leaf is single-axis, knots are the all-words-distinct values). Installed: ATOMG <- atomg, ATOM <- atom on axis cache_line_count (replaces the r1 / r2 atomic_same_address_lanes tables: those were the 32-distinct-lines pattern, 61.6 / 67.6 (h100) and 58.1 / 55.3 (b300) at every L); RED / REDG keep r3. Gate history: the r2-r4 increment gates were not met by returning atomics (concave issue back-pressure window) although the value reproduced; the r5 gate was redefined with user authorisation before this run.

barrier_release.h100.r4.description: H100 barrier_release protocol v2 (tools/microbench/barrier_release/protocol-v2.json + addendum 2026-11-05; probes verbatim, --reps 256 --launches 8, two runs; sm_90a runs only the mbarrier cells of sync_mb / sync_xw -- the tcgen05 cells are unrealised there). mbarrier.release = E[t_w - t_s | try_wait waiter, delay >= 4000] - o_s - o_w - r_sync = 87.93 (run a 88.27 / b 87.60, se 0.54 each, agreement 0.8 %; r13 value 88.30 from h100-r1/r2) -> measured. cta.release(W) = E[bar.cta.wW.warplast] - o_s(12) - o_w(7) = 16.0 for W = 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 in both runs (se 0; W = 2 / 32 negative: phase wrap, reported) -> measured, same as crossings.cta_release.h100.r1. cluster.release(S) = E[bar.cluster.cS.relaxed.arriver] - o_s(28) - o_w(13) = 86 / 81 / 81 for S = 2 / 4 / 8 (deterministic in both runs) -> measured; the .release arrive form measures 739 / 731 / 731 (MEMBAR.ALL.GPU + ERRBAR before UCGABAR_ARV, ~650 cycles of fence, reported, not installed); replaces the hopper-prototype fit 164-202 (hopper.cluster.sync.release). cp_async.arrival = (median noinc - issue) - (median arrive - issue) = 15.5 (16 / 15, se 1.5, agreement 6.5 % > 5 %) -> experimental (r13 value 18.0 from h100-r1).

constant_launch.h100.r3.description: H100 constant_launch protocols v2 + v3 (tools/microbench/constant_launch/protocol-v2.json, protocol-v3.json, frozen before data; probes constlaunch_v2.cu / constlaunch_v3.cu: 16 dependent constant loads per traversal, two traversals, CS2R after every load, ncu --cache-control all, 34 launches, first 2 dropped, two runs; per-load latency = clock delta minus the installed result latency of the single in-between op (IMAD / USHF 4)). Uniform path (ULDC / LDCU with UR index, v3 run h100-r3): bank-0 first 288.5 (experimental), second 68.0 (measured); bank-3 first 270.0 (experimental), second 68.0 (measured) -> no uniform rule (declared condition: both measured and second within 10 % of first); uniform loads keep the miss / hit / same-line / in-flight rules. Cold miss: vector bank-3 first 817.2 (measured) vs uniform 270.0 (experimental) -> miss_latency_cycles unchanged (declared condition: both measured and within 10 %). Not installed (A/B arms only): the v2 'every bank-0 access' rule (task/lifecycle-v3 913d77d, arm $A/merge/cbi).

crossings.constant_cache.h100.r2.description: H100 crossings protocol v2 constant_cache cell (tools/microbench/crossings/protocol-v2.json; probe ldc_chain.cu: register-indexed LDC pointer chase over a 64 KiB __constant__ table, strides 4/64/128/256 B, footprints 256 B-64 KiB, U 64/256, warm = reps >= 1, cold = first traversal after cudaMemcpyToSymbol; per-load latency = OLS slope over U, two runs agree within 0.07 %). Two warm levels: 37.0 cycles up to the 2 KiB L0 knee at every stride, 107.2 beyond it up to the whole 64 KiB bank (no capacity knee inside the bank, capacity_bytes kept at the bank size); same_line = warm S 4 / F 256 B = 37.0; line_bytes = 64 (the smallest stride whose warm latency equals the hit plateau within 5 % of the S4-to-plateau step; S 4 averages 96.1); miss = cold first traversal at S 256 B / F 64 KiB where every one of the 256 loads touches a new line = 406.5 (the other cold cells mix first-touch and re-touch within the chain: S64 F16/32/64 KiB 136.3/206.6/293.0, S128 F32/64 KiB 219.8/316.1). Verdict measured. Replaces same_line 28.02 / hit 93.89 / miss 382.45 / line 256 / capacity 65536 (hopper-prototype ccscan/constcold/paramwarm harness fits, no probe in this repository). Note (engine, 2026-11-05): MemoryHierarchy::constant() keeps a constant line resident for one cycle only (l1_resident_ shared with the data-L1 fallback), so every LDC pays miss until task/constant-cache-residency lands.

dispatch_refill.h100.r4.description: dispatch_refill run 4 (protocol.json addendum 5). Refill gap per SM class over the six spin cells of runs 1, 2, 4 (three cards): fast 150.3 ns (147.0-154.7), slow 183.5 ns (180.5-187.7); the slow class is four whole topology gpcs, {1,2,3,7} on three of the four cards measured and {1,2,3,5} on one -- the mask is the majority set, a declared choice. PREEXIT: a CTA in which it was executed occupies the dispatch serializer for 0.95 x serial_ns_per_cta more (0.586 ns); per CTA, linear in the fraction of CTAs, independent of position and launch attribute; replay within 2.5 % on all 18 cells. The earlier 174.92 ns (hopper-prototype, tail mode) lies between the two classes.

dsmem.h100.unreachable.description: STRUCTURAL unreachable record (dsmem protocol, tools/microbench/dsmem/protocol.json): on sm_90a, ld / st.shared::cluster to a peer CTA (and to the own rank through the cluster window) compile to generic LD.E / ST.E, exactly as on sm_103a, so LDS / STS / STSM never carry a peer rank and the remote_smem = 1 children of storage.shared.{visibility, issue, acceptance_sm} are never selected; the corpus agrees (0 executed LDS / STS / STSM / LD / ST with a peer rank in the 450 single-cluster cases; peer DSMEM traffic is STAS and remote SYNCS arrives, with their own leaves). Values kept as sentinels (visibility 290.03 = hopper-prototype remote dependent-load fit; issue / acceptance 41.24 = hopper-prototype steady cells). Measured for reference, both runs identical: peer ld.shared::cluster dependent-load latency 206.5 cycles (b300 220.5), own rank through the cluster window 51.0 (b300 51.0), plain LDS chain 33.8 (both). Open engine item: own-CTA generic LD / ST in the cluster shared window are marked space shared_cluster and the segment builder maps that code to generic, so the engine times them through the global memory hierarchy.

ifetch.h100.r1.mix.description: H100 fetch_parallelism from the version-1 run's k_mix variants (W warps on W distinct straight-line bodies) per the protocol-v2 addendum of 2026-11-05 (blackwell-prototype rules F7 / F8, the rule behind the b300 value): warm passes, cpi_line_L2 5.536 (k_line W=1 L2 plateau 160-512 KiB, a0 21), k_mix points with total footprint > capacity_l1 114688 B: q(4) = 1.081 / 1.115 (p = 4 / q(4) = 3.70 / 3.59: four warps on four SMSPs each get nearly their own stream cadence), q(8) = 1.424 / 1.446, q(16) = 1.882 / 1.935 (modes all / none, agreement 3.1 / 1.5 / 2.8 %); streams per SMSP = round(4 / q(16) = 2.10) = 2 -> 8 arrival channels per SM (warp-slot indexed). Experimental: F8 intermediate verdict, the channel form gives q(8) = 1 and q(16) = 2 against the measured 1.44 / 1.91; the H100 figures coincide with the B300 ones (mechtree.ifetch.r3: p 3.57-3.75, q(8) 1.37-1.42, q(16) 1.83-1.86) but are derived from H100 data only. Replaces the unrealised placeholder 1 (k_jump never built); the 128 KiB total-footprint k_mix point (w4.n2048, none mode, q 0.39) sits on the L1 transition like k_line 128 KiB and is kept in the median per the frozen rule without changing it.

Version-1 plateau rules: L0 28672 B, L1 114688 B, line 128 B, launch prefetch 65536 B (two-segment engine-form knot, both runs), sharing 0 (W = 4 warm cpi within 10 % of W = 1) -> measured.

ifetch.h100.r4.experimental.description: Same run, marginal-slope form: stream_l1 = OLS slope of T_warm over lines for L0 < F <= L1 = 19.62 (runs identical), stream_l2 = slope for F > L1 = 49.37 (runs within 0.5 %), stream_cold = free slope above the 64 KiB knot of the engine-form two-segment fit of T_0 = 120.77 (runs within 0.8 %). Experimental per protocol: the slope fits' max relative residual exceeds 5 % (the transition footprints next to each capacity sit on the fitted range) and the engine-form prediction inside the prefetched head is 12-13 % above the measured pass-0 cycles (the launch prefetch streams faster than the warm L1 cadence): per-F T0/pred (rel) 8K 564/628 (11 %), 16K 1664/1883 (13 %), 20K 2228/2511 (13 %), 24K 2792/3138 (12 %), 28K 3330/3766 (13 %), 32K 3894/4394 (13 %), 48K 6132/6905 (13 %), 64K 8850/9415 (6 %), 80K 23730/24814 (5 %), 96K 39823/40212 (1 %), 112K 55699/55610 (0 %), 128K 71128/71008 (0 %), 160K 103187/101805 (1 %), 192K 133931/132601 (1 %), 256K 196632/194194 (1 %), 512K 438885/440566 (0 %). Replaces the version-1 cpi-difference values 9.30 / 36.29 / 72.04 (ifetch.h100.r1.experimental), which the protocol v2 superseded because the two forms disagreed.

ifetch.h100.v3.description: ifetch protocol v3 (tools/microbench/ifetch/protocol-v3.json): looped straight-line code of 224-384 lines, warm passes. No miss up to 248 lines; 34 / 76 / 110 / 155 / 197 / 275 missed lines at 256 / 264 / 272 / 280 / 288 / 304 lines (9.3 cycles per line), every line from 320 on: five misses per line over capacity, saturating 64 lines later = a 4-way cache of 64 sets (32 KiB; the loop's own 8-10 lines share it). The earlier 28672 B was the last plateau cell of the coarser v1 sweep. Four warps on the same code give the same numbers.

l1_residency.h100.r2.description: H100 l1_residency protocol v4 (tools/microbench/crossings/l1_residency/protocol-v4.json; probe l1cap.cu v3: one CTA, lane-0 dependent ld.global.ca chase over F = 4..256 KiB in 4 KiB steps, random cyclic 128 B lines, warm then timed pass; --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs, SASS gate ok). The L1 data budget of a launch is set by the shared-memory configuration the driver selects (occupancy rule: smallest supported configuration >= n_res x (dynamic + static + 1 KiB), n_res = min(32 CTAs, 64 warps / block warps, 228 KiB / per-CTA need)), not by the launch's own shared bytes: the 10 default-hint cells (S 0 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 192 KiB x block 32 / 1024) give effective capacity E = 184 / 240 / 20 / 148 / 52 / 116 / 116 / 116 / 52 / 52 KiB with configurations 64 / 8 / 228 / 100 / 196 / 132 / 132 / 132 / 196 / 196 KiB (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor equals n_res in every cell) and E + configuration = 248 KiB in all 10 cells of both runs (spread 0) -> data_array_bytes = 253952, reserved_bytes = 0 (measured; the 8 KiB below 256 KiB is the unusable part of the array, the same on both devices). The pinned-hint cells (v3 install path, unrealised) show that cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout does not pin the configuration (hint 0 / 4 / 8 / >= 15 % -> 8 / 100 / 164 / 228 KiB at S = 0; 44 % -> 228 at S = 0 but 132 at S = 64 KiB). Replaces the hopper-prototype residency-fit pair 262144 / 8192 (hopper.141c7baf1efeaffc74458450 / hopper.145407ce83c814fd79fd55d8), whose difference 253952 this run reproduces exactly; the engine value is unchanged. Engine finding handed to the engine line: l1_cap_lines should subtract the selected configuration, not the launch's shared bytes.

l2_merge.h100.async_kernel_check.description: cp.async joins the GPC read domain on h100 (domain_gpc = 2), by the kernel check declared in tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol-v2.json addendum h100_async_kernel_check_2: eight kernels with hardware L2 counters, mean absolute difference of reads per delivered sector 0.183 with the pair domain, 0.114 with the GPC domain (GPC with the 21.75-cycle window 0.158, pair with it 0.236, GPC with the window counted from the shared read service 0.175). The pair domain shares nothing on triton_grouped_gemm_02 / 03 (1.06 / 1.11 against 0.648 / 0.430 on hardware; GPC 0.672 / 0.478). Counterexamples kept: cutlass_dense_cpasync_05 / 06 share 0.24 more than hardware with the GPC domain (0.671 / 0.635 against 0.911 / 0.880), flashinfer_single_prefill_02 0.13 more. Replaces the hopper-prototype full-GPU scan values window 235 (hopper.cd0cd6500f88dc4a4202a80d, same M6 r2 method, reproduced) and max_requests 3 (hopper.3667abe72c627f7114c32123: N = 3 vs 4 was within 0.02 MAE there too); delivered_bytes_per_cycle keeps hopper.17a05956f82b13ac352f95d5 (M1 r4 LDG lockstep 25.2 TB/s).

l2_merge.h100.r3.delivered.description: H100 l2_merge protocol v2 (tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol-v2.json; probe ldg_scan.cu = hopper-prototype l2_dram_scan_microbench.cu at 16c47f74 verbatim except the SM-count bound and the CUDA 13 clock attributes; sass gate PASS scan_kernel<false> LDG.E.128 x8; set m1r4: 132 SMs, 24 MB L2-resident footprint split into 132/G slices, G CTAs per slice stream the same 256 MB in lockstep with 1024 threads of ld.global.cg.v4; two runs x 5 trials, every config once under ncu). delivered_bytes_per_cycle = max over the lock configs of the SM-side aggregate per SM cycle = 12807.1 / 12691.1 (run-a / run-b, agree 0.9 %), both at ld_l2g_24mb_g004_lock (25.36 / 25.13 TB/s at 1980 MHz; r = lts/l1tex bytes 0.298, i.e. 70 % of the delivered bytes were merged; dram read 12 MB = L2-resident). ldl.h100.memory_hierarchy.description: STRUCTURAL: LDL timing is owned by the memory hierarchy. The converter gives every LDL a local-space memory reference and the engine sends space-local accesses through MemoryHierarchy::load (cpp/core/simulator.cpp memory-access branch: only spaces 1 shared / 3 constant leave that path), so the load-to-use latency comes from the memory.l1 / l2 / dram leaves. Corpus check (executed warp instructions in the single-cluster facts): hopper 9302 LDL in 115 cases, blackwell 16229 in 69 cases, every one with lane addresses (MACC sectors), none without. The previous value 50.504 was a collapsed predecessor table cell (service_latency.h100.r1.table_collapse, experimental) and is replaced by the owner rule's 1 / 1, as on b300.

lsu_accept.h100.v5r1.description: H100 lsu_accept protocol v5 (tools/microbench/lsu_accept/protocol-v5.json; probe store_queue.cu: one CTA, W in {1,2,4,8} warps on distinct SMSPs, 24 back-to-back st.global per warp on distinct pointer registers with a %clock64 read after every store, --launches 16 --reps 65, two runs). mechtree.w6.memory.default_load_cache_po.description: B300/SM103 default scalar ld.global.u32 matches explicit ca, native enum 0=cache_all (cpp/src/memory.cpp). cache-policy50: GPU-800b87ec-59fe-6b25-eedf-a036db9ce10c and GPU-fa241899-7f9c-9a20-9a48-45a5362c6346; B300 SXM6 AC, CC10.3, driver 580.159.03, nvcc/cuobjdump 13.2.78, NCU 2026.1.1.0. Three controls x 4 launches x 2 independent GPUs. Each launch: 8 single-warp CTAs x 128 dependent scalar loads, 1024 requests/4096 sectors. Default and ca each give 4064 hits/32 misses; cg gives 0 hits/4096 misses on every launch. SASS: LDG.E / LDG.E.STRONG.SM / LDG.E.STRONG.GPU, one load in the 128-iteration address-feedback loop, no clock reads or spills; poisoned uint64 lane outputs all validate, CUDA UUIDs match NVML. No -dlcm override. Only LSU counters used, not profiler timing; no cache-line size, residency/capacity, queue-depth or latency inference. Raw warnings and frozen counter model are retained.

mechtree.w6.memory.sector_bytes.description: B300/SM103 LSU scalar u32 global cg load/store coalescing sector: 32 bytes. Independent load and store scans each cover 10 address strides/offsets x 4 launches x 2 GPUs (80 launches/direction), 8 single-warp CTAs x 128 instructions per launch; all request/sector counts exactly match byte-address sector partitions. SASS: one scalar LDG or STG in each loop, no clock reads, zero spills; unprofiled/profiled full-output checks pass and CUDA UUIDs match NVML. Load cache-sector44: GPU-fa241899-7f9c-9a20-9a48-45a5362c6346 and GPU-4221633a-c6ad-c451-8bb0-79ceac1bb786; store cache-sector-store47: GPU-800b87ec-59fe-6b25-eedf-a036db9ce10c and GPU-4221633a-c6ad-c451-8bb0-79ceac1bb786. B300 SXM6 AC, CC10.3, driver 580.159.03, nvcc/cuobjdump 13.2.78, NCU 2026.1.1.0. Only LSU request/sector counts are used; no profiler timing, cache-line size, policy, residency, queue depth or bandwidth is inferred. Recorded hwloc warnings remain in the evidence. The value builder reads frozen load/store models, never re-fits the raw captures.

mechtree.w9.l2cnt.line_bytes.description: EXPERIMENTAL B300 L2 allocation granularity 128 B: probes/l2cnt.cu counter-only (ncu --cache-control none, two GPUs GPU-0380f7e8-4ce6-a5d0-7eb9-10d8c3ad9574 / GPU-bcb6d477-2441-4742-bdca-071716ceb43e, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.2.78, run l2cnt-113 commit f856dbd3): every SM walks F distinct 128 B lines with ld.global.cg touching one sector of each line (P1) or all four (P4), warm then measured pass. A missing 1-sector request costs four L2 read-miss sectors like a full-line request (P1 misses = 4F at F >= 2M lines), and the miss curves over F = 128K..3M lines coincide (line-level hit 1.000/0.995/0.84/0.21/0.02 at 0.4/0.5/0.66/0.79/1.0 M lines for both patterns, memq_rules.same_line_curves true on both GPUs). Experimental because lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read_lookup_hit reads 0 on this part, so the curves use 1 - misses/(4F) instead of the hit counter the rule was written for.

store_flood.h100.r1.description: store_flood protocol v1: 384 lane stores per warp in 48 unrolled groups of 8 with a %clock64 read after each group, W in {1,2,4,8} issuing warps on one SM. Steady-state service per request T = max(floor, sectors + P): P counts the touched 128-B lines containing a partially written 32-B granule, floor 2.0 cycles per request (issue_interval), proportional to W (one service per SM). Installs store_l2.partial_line_cycles = 1.0, store_l2.partial_granule_bytes = 32, store_l2.issue_interval_cycles = 2.0; the measured buffer range 32.6-61.4 covers the installed outstanding_requests 43, which is kept. Experimental until the protocol's engine replay passes.

store_scatter.h100.r1.description: store_scatter protocol v1, committed before GPU data (8267a101). Twenty-four stores with clock reads between stores, distinct address registers; widths 2/4/8/16 B x lane strides width/32/128 B x W=1/2, 16 launches x 64 retained repetitions, two runs. Early issue interval = median gaps 2..4 minus (clock-only gap 2 - 1): 3/3/6/23 cycles, identical across all address geometries, both W and both runs. Contiguous controls reproduce lsu_accept v5. Late queue backpressure depends on geometry and is deliberately not installed as an issue interval. This separates width from sector count, confounded in the original contiguous-only experiment.

structural.execution_units.description: Execution units shared by both architectures (mechanism-merge-plan 2.1): one copy per scope, modelled by the service leaf's issue_interval_cycles (initiation interval) and an optional measured in-flight cap (max_inflight_per_copy, 0 = none). The resource's own initiation_interval_cycles field is not read by the engine (kept 1).

structural.generic_shared_alias.description: generic-pointer LD/ST that resolve to (cluster) shared memory take the LSU shared path of LDS/STS; leaf values alias the LDS/STS points, no new measurement. Corpus (old 450x2 facts, $A/diag/mb4/dyncount-{hp,bw}.tsv): LD->shared_cluster hp 3011 inst / 46 cases, bw 0; ST hp 976 / 8, bw 7424 / 17; ATOM/ATOMS->shared_cluster 0 on both devices, so ATOMS stays owned by storage.atomic.issue alone.

structural.issue_group.dispatch_slot.artifact: hopper-prototype cpp/src/engine.cpp (reserve_resource(issue_group, 0, 0.0, warp, now, now + 1)); cyclescope cpp/core/simulator.cpp try_issue (which = 1 loop) and scheduler.policy issue_slots = 1
structural.issue_group.dispatch_slot.description: STRUCTURAL: the predecessor's issue_group_resource (smsp_compute_register_issue) was a per-SMSP dispatch slot reserved for exactly ONE cycle per instance (occupancy now..now+1, interval 0), i.e. the 1 warp-instruction per SMSP per cycle rule that cyclescope already enforces through scheduler.policy.issue_slots = 1. The import bound these 68 classes (FFMA / FADD / FMUL / IADD3 / IMAD / LOP3 / ISETP / FMNMX / MUFU / F2FP / SHFL / S2R / ... plus the U* classes) to uniform_smsp as a second unit, and cyclescope's engine occupies the second unit for the class's own issue_interval (the b300 second-pipe semantics: FFMA2 holds fmaheavy for ~2 cycles), so every ALU / FMA / XU instruction of an SMSP serialised on one unit at 1-8.3 cycles each (MUFU 8.26 blocked a following FADD): a porting defect, not a measured mechanism. Evidence on the single-cluster ledgers (ifp arm, build-main10): fa3_fwd_features_03 RWAIT uniform_smsp 213,894 of 182,572 resource-wait cycles (consumer warps 29 %/warp), flashinfer_sampling_00 370,823, flashmla_dense_decode 32,113 of 37,890; with the binding removed the same cases drop 4-20 % and the uniform_smsp wait falls to 1-3 k (U* classes only). The binding is now none for these classes, as on b300 (structural.service_owner), the class's own unit (field resource, common/class_resource.json) remains; the U* classes keep resource = uniform_smsp.

structural.nanosleep_requested.description: PTX nanosleep: the warp suspends for the requested duration (requested_sleep_cycles = ns folded to cycles by the converter), slope 1; both architectures.

structural.pmtrig.no_result.artifact: SASS: PMTRIG is the performance-monitor trigger (cuBLAS / CUTLASS kernels emit it around the main loop); it produces no register result and is consumed by no instruction
structural.pmtrig.no_result.description: STRUCTURAL: PMTRIG retires on the issue frontend in one cycle with no unit, no result latency and no interval — the same ownership rule as the control classes (NOP / YIELD) of service_latency protocol-v2 ownership_rule 'control'.

structural.predicated_off.description: STRUCTURAL: a predicated-off instance retires in one cycle on the issue frontend with no unit, no in-flight cap and no interval, on both devices (the b300 leaf carried max_inflight 1 from the predecessor).

structural.scheduler.policy_switch.description: STRUCTURAL: engine scheduling-policy switches, not timing quantities. cursor_commit = 1: the per-SMSP issue cursor advances past the warp that issued (loose round-robin); try_next_on_block = 1: a warp that cannot issue this cycle hands the slot to the next eligible warp instead of stalling the SMSP. Both are modelling choices of the issue loop (no microbenchmark can isolate them from the per-class service leaves); they replace the hopper-prototype copies ('same physical endpoint and numeric value', experimental) and placeholder.p0. The former eligible_policy / yield_policy fields had no read point in the engine and were removed.

structural.service_owner.description: STRUCTURAL owner rule: the service leaf of a class whose timing is owned by another mechanism (memory.* hierarchy, storage.* TMA / shared / atomic, tensor.pipe) is 1 / 1 / 0 with no cap; predicated-off and unmeasured fields of newly added classes likewise. Also cited by the hopper queue_class field previously sourced from dce10c72aa13.

structural.v10.memory.model_version.description: V10 initialized memory configuration requires model_version=1 in job validation. This enum identifies the supported software model/serialization format, not a B300 timing or geometry measurement. Sector bytes, line bytes, cache policies and capacity fields retain their independent evidence; the validator requiring a geometry value does not measure it.

tensor_pipe.h100.completion.experimental.description: H100 tensor.completion = single-op latency (lat U=1 minus U=0 minus SASS o_s difference) - pipe beat: ss 9 cycles (IGMMA 7) above n 16, rs ~ -1 -> 0; negative values beyond 2 se (ss n 8 / 16, all rs) installed as 0 with pipe = beat (protocol-v2 addendum). Experimental because the U=0 baseline kernel contains the compiler's null HGMMA for the empty commit group, so the baseline is not a pure commit.

tensor_pipe.h100.completion.ser.r4.description: h100-r4 serialized-latency cells (ser): U x {wgmma.fence; 1 op same D; commit; wait_group 0}, U in {1,2,4,8}; L_ser = OLS slope, completion_ser = L_ser - beat - o_ser (o_ser = per-iteration non-target SASS issue stalls from control words). Acceptance: max fit residual <= 2% and run-a/run-b agreement <= 3%/2 cycles -> measured. grp cells (4 ops per group, bf16/e4m3e4m3 ss n in {64,128,256}) agree with ser within 0.25% confirming the engine group rule. 483 cells passed, 0 experimental, 1 cell without ser data untouched.

tensor_pipe.h100.r1h.description: H100 tensor_pipe protocol v2 (tools/microbench/tensor_pipe/probe/wgmma*.cu, new probe generated by probe/gen_wgmma.py: one warpgroup, operands in SMEM with no-swizzle K-major descriptors, every ISA-valid n, HGMMA f16 (F32/F16 accumulators) / bf16 / tf32, QGMMA e4m3.e4m3 / e4m3.e5m2 / e5m2.e5m2, IGMMA s8.s8; two runs per cell). tensor.pipe = OLS slope of the cadence over U {32,64,128} (n/2 cycles above n 32, floor 18 / 20 at n 8 / 16; the two-warpgroup diagnostic gives 2.00x, one pipe per SM). ss cells (A from SMEM), run h100-r1h, SASS gate on dumps from the extracted cubins.

tensor_pipe.h100.r1h.experimental.description: H100 tensor_pipe protocol v2 (tools/microbench/tensor_pipe/probe/wgmma*.cu, new probe generated by probe/gen_wgmma.py: one warpgroup, operands in SMEM with no-swizzle K-major descriptors, every ISA-valid n, HGMMA f16 (F32/F16 accumulators) / bf16 / tf32, QGMMA e4m3.e4m3 / e4m3.e5m2 / e5m2.e5m2, IGMMA s8.s8; two runs per cell). tensor.pipe = OLS slope of the cadence over U {32,64,128} (n/2 cycles above n 32, floor 18 / 20 at n 8 / 16; the two-warpgroup diagnostic gives 2.00x, one pipe per SM). ss cells whose U {32,64,128} fit residual exceeds 2 % (e5m2.e5m2 n 120: 2.5 %, tf32 n 232: 1.4 % with run disagreement); installed as experimental.

tensor_pipe.h100.r3.description: H100 tensor_pipe protocol v2 (tools/microbench/tensor_pipe/probe/wgmma*.cu, new probe generated by probe/gen_wgmma.py: one warpgroup, operands in SMEM with no-swizzle K-major descriptors, every ISA-valid n, HGMMA f16 (F32/F16 accumulators) / bf16 / tf32, QGMMA e4m3.e4m3 / e4m3.e5m2 / e5m2.e5m2, IGMMA s8.s8; two runs per cell). tensor.pipe = OLS slope of the cadence over U {32,64,128} (n/2 cycles above n 32, floor 18 / 20 at n 8 / 16; the two-warpgroup diagnostic gives 2.00x, one pipe per SM). rs cells (A from registers), run h100-r3: the cad window is a runtime loop over a 16-op body (protocol addendum; the straight-line r1h / r2c windows were serialized by ptxas, C7511), no C7511, SASS gate per loop body.

tensor_pipe.h100.r6.sp.description: tensor_pipe h100-r6 sparse wgmma (.sp k32/k64): beat + completion_ser, 191/192 measured

tma_cold.h100.r1.description: H100 tma_cold protocol run r1 (tools/microbench/tma_cold/protocol.json; blackwell-prototype tma.cu verbatim, dc1 SWIZZLE_128B rank-2 tile UTMALDG, U back-to-back under one expect_tx, hot = 512 KiB tensor, cold = new rows of a 512 MiB tensor each rep; two runs x 16 launches x 32 reps, n = 512 per cell). cycles = L2-hot completion (E[t_w-t_s | 1 TMA] - o_s) - (E[.. | arrive] - o_s) per box, every knot measured (se <= 1.1 %, runs within 1.3 %). cold_extra_cycles = cold - hot per box: 128:446, 256:238, 512:246, 1024:232, 2048:261, 4096:278, 8192:312, 16384:322, 32768:332; knots 16384 B experimental (run agreement 3.2-3.5 %), leaf experimental. Replaces the predecessor Hopper rows of mixed provenance for the tile dc1 leaf.

tma_cold.h100.r1.prior.description: Family-shared prior: the dc1 tile cold_extra knots applied by transfer_bytes to the multicast (destination_count >= 2) and non-tile (gather4 / im2col) UTMALDG leaves, which the tma_cold protocol does not measure (same rule the predecessor used for the hot leaf; protocol install section).

tma_forms.h100.r3.description: tma_forms protocol v2 (+ addenda) h100 run h100-r3: variant table -> (class,form,direction); completion = E[tw-ts|U1]-E[tw-ts|U0] minus issue offsets (own-destination t_w = completion_own for dc>1); service = OLS slope over U; UBLKCP dc0-1 knots from s->g store cells with load-direction comparison; replaced old values recorded per leaf

tma_forms.h100.r4.description: tma_forms v3/r4h: UBLKCP load-direction (.S.G) knots at 1/4/16/32KiB with restored U=0 control (plain arrive + waiter spin); multicast load cell not realised (runtime failure) so the dc2+ load leaf keeps the knots copied from the identity partition

tma_forms.h100.r5.description: H100 tma_forms r5 (protocol-v3 + 2026-11-05 addendum). Reproduces the r4 UBLKCP load dc 0-1 knots within the v1 bound (service 71.91 / 71.84 / 255.40 / 506.67 vs installed 71.6 / 71.4 / 254.2 / 506.6; completion 317.69 / 362.93 / 555.85 / 809.77 vs 309.5 / 358.0 / 554.5 / 807.8, largest difference 2.6 % at 1 KiB), so the r4 values stay. Multicast load (dc 4 within 6 % of dc 2 -> one dc 2+ leaf): completion 4 / 16 KiB = 435.20 / 580.66 (completion_own, rank 0).

tma_forms.h100.r5.experimental.description: Same run: multicast load service 4 / 16 KiB = 58.92 / 255.86 (slope over U in {1, 2, 4}, se 11-16 cycles).

tma_oob.h100.v2r1.artifact: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/tma_oob/h100-v2r1 (run-a/b.jsonl, 78+78 rows, no error); protocol tools/microbench/tma_oob/protocol-v2.json addendum
tma_oob.h100.v2r1.description: tma_oob v2: a tiled TMA load whose box is cut along dimension 0 completes +178 cycles and owes the SM 2.02 cycles of service per in-bounds row (cap at 128 rows extrapolated); whole rows outside (other dims) cost nothing; fully outside not modelled. Installs storage.tma.completion cut_extra_cycles = 178 and storage.async.service_start cut_service_cycles = 2.02 x cut_rows.

tma_store_loaded.h100.gpc_scope.description: Per-GPC limits of the L2 read service and of the store service (tma_store_loaded protocol-v5 addenda gpc_scope / gpc_scope_result / gpc_scope_replay): unshared cp.async reads of the SMs of one GPC reach 1.06 TB/s at 8, 12 and 18 SMs (two runs identical), every SM 7.78 TB/s; reduce TMA stores of one GPC reach 0.53 TB/s at 12 and 18 SMs, plain stores 0.66-0.70 (runs 6 percent apart), so the plain-store value is the reduce limit x 1.25 = 0.663 TB/s (the measured reduce / plain ratio of the GPC limits is 0.75, of the per-SM rates 0.80). Engine replay of the traced cells with these values: per-SM rate 1.01 (stores, one GPC), 0.98 (stores, every SM), 1.03 (reads, one GPC), 0.95 (reads, every SM) of hardware; without them 1.71 and 3.41 on the one-GPC cells.

tma_store_loaded.h100.r6.description: MEASURED H100 (GPU-4a698cd4, driver 570.124.06; tools/microbench/tma_store_loaded/protocol-v4.json, run h100-r6, artifact microbench/tma_store_loaded/h100-r6, model fg-gemm/tsl/h100-v4-model.json): on one SM fill sectors (TMA tile loads, plain LDG) and store sectors (TMA store drain, STG) take turns on one port. Port occupancy computed with the installed rates (store_l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle 31.65, l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle 122.31) is 0.993-1.020 in the 12 slowed pairs and 0.71 / 0.86 in the 2 unslowed ones, runs a / b equal to three digits. Criterion adjusted after data (protocol-v4 addendum 2026-11-10). Structural switch, value 1.

tma_store_loaded.h100.r6.shared_store.description: fills and synchronous shared-store acceptance (and the dirty proxy-fence drain) take turns on the per-SM memory port: protocol-v4 recorded U 0.980-0.995 for sts + load pairs on both devices; hw-extra rounds with four TMA load slots match acceptance + fill port time within 2 percent; recorded there as R2, not a predeclared install form

tma_store_loaded.h100.store_dest.description: MEASURED H100 (GPU-ebc96a9f-c7b3-c18e-f7fa-d5f9e76a6c04, driver 570.124.06; tools/microbench/tma_store_loaded/protocol-v5.json addendum, run fg-line-sync/store-dest/h100-r1, SASS gate 4/4): a TMA reduce-add store (UTMAREDG) costs 640.9 vs 512.9 cycles per 16 KiB vs a plain store on one SM (ratio 1.25) on the SM store port and the shared L2-write service, and with a destination not resident in L2 every byte is fetched from DRAM first; the bulk group completes no earlier than that fetch. Taken over by the shared-memory line without the fetch hold (tma_store_loaded protocol-v5 addendum reduce_rule_scope); the ratio also applies to the per-GPC store service.

trywait_wake.h100.r1.description: H100 trywait_wake protocol run r1 (tools/microbench/trywait_wake/protocol.json; pod mb-trywaitw-h100-r1, $A/microbench/trywait_wake/h100-r1, model $A/fg-fix5/r4/h100-wake-model.json): two-warp probe, waiter suspended in mbarrier.try_wait, completer arrives D cycles later; wake = resume - completion. try_wait form D >= 200: 203 / 239 / 269 / 195 / 218 / 246 (arrive) and 203 / 243 / 269 / 192 / 218 / 245 (complete_tx), mean 228.3; suspendTimeHint form 194 (arrive) / 208 (tx) flat over D; runs agree. The test_wait spin control gives 140-225 (median 173.5), not the installed release 87.9 (which came from a same-thread arrive -> try_wait chain that never blocks), so the protocol control fails by construction -> installed as experimental; the cross-warp release itself is to be re-measured by a barrier_release revision.

wgmma_handoff.h100.r1c.description: H100 wgmma_handoff r1c (tools/microbench/wgmma_handoff/protocol.json): FFMA reading the first accumulator register of a just-completed wgmma (after wgmma.wait_group D) vs the same FFMA reading an ordinary register, observed by a dependent FADD; 8 producer forms (HGMMA 64x64/64x128/64x192 bf16|f16 ss, 64x128 bf16 rs, 64x128x8 tf32; QGMMA e4m3 64x128/136/192x32) x group_depth D 0-3, SASS gate 64/64. E_acc = E_ctrl in every cell (6 cycles at D 0, 8 at D 1-3, both runs identical) -> handoff 0 at every depth and form: no accumulator handoff delay beyond the async-group wait. Replaces the hopper-prototype placeholders (D 0-1: 0 / disabled, temporary.65d0df53fc929744660515b2) and the three predecessor QGMMA F32.E4M3.E4M3 ss 64xNx32 points at D >= 2 (N 136 / 152 / 192: 111.8 / 139.1 / 74.7 cycles, native-profile handoff_contention_cycles, measurement_verified false; N 136 and 192 were remeasured here: 0).

wgmma_overlap.h100.r7.description: H100 wgmma_overlap r7 (protocol v5; same overlap_v3.cu probe as r6: kernel operand-form streams ffma_ur / ffma_ur_r / fmul_ur / fmul_r / fadd1 / fadd2n / ilp8 / ilp8n / f2fp / mufu8, 176/192 SASS gate; f2fp unrealised - ptxas desugars into LOP3.LUT/FADD helper insts). Verdict C3+C7 experimental (pass_frac 0.895, max_err 0.59); C3+C7+R measured (1.0 pass, max_err 0.465). Facts: uniform-register operands are free (ffma_ur / fmul_ur t ~= 2.0-2.6 same as fadd1); any instruction carrying a .reuse source flag costs 3.75-4.13 regardless of reads (reuse_flag_floor 4); every op with A in registers (rs) adds alternating +0/+1 on the issuing warpgroup's issues (rs_extra_half_cycles; rs cells: 2.54-2.59 on 2-read, 4.05 on reuse-flagged, ilp8n 3.59); f2fp unrealised; mufu8 9.38 vs base 8.19 (+1.2 unmodelled). Installed: cycles 2, enabled 1, coresident_dependent_half_cycles 1, reuse_flag_floor_cycles 4, rs_extra_half_cycles 1.

wgmma_overlap.h100.v6.description: wgmma_overlap protocol v6 (tools/microbench/wgmma_overlap/protocol-v6.json, addenda 1-6; probe overlap_v4.cu; runs $A/fg-line-cold/wov6/h100-r{1..5}). Launch hold: with one op per commit group the issue of G ops ends at max(21 G, (G - 6) x op time) (n128: 89 / 129 / 169 / 263 / 391 / 1159 cycles for G = 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 / 24); with three or six ops per group it is not held (251.5 / 491.5 for G = 12 / 24) -> six pending commit groups. Memory-queue hold: MUFU.EX2, MUFU.RSQ, SHFL.BFLY and shared loads on the SMSPs of the issuing warpgroup's warps -- of another warpgroup's warp and of the owner alike -- do not issue until about seven (6.3-8.8) of its ops are left, whatever the commit grouping (first MUFU / SHFL of the other warp 1144 / 1165 cycles after its window start with six / one op per group, G = 24; FFMA from the first cycle). Not modelled: MUFU 10 against 8.4 cycles after the hold; ops take about 80 instead of 64.5 cycles while another warp runs on the SMSP; two warpgroups issuing at once; Blackwell not measured. The rule first installed from runs 1-3 (launch hold counted ops) was wrong for multi-op groups and is replaced. Installed: only the launch hold (six pending commit groups). The memory-queue hold is measured for one issuing warpgroup but is not installed (both fields 0): run 6 (three warpgroups in a ring, $A/fg-line-cold/wov6/h100-r6) shows that with several issuing warpgroups the engine's op timeline differs from the hardware's (each warpgroup waits about 465 cycles for its first commit group whether or not other warpgroups' ops are in flight; a 15-op section takes 126 cycles alone and 200-1000 in the ring), so the hold would be applied at the wrong times.
